section: Sufism - doctrines, khanqah, sama; silsilas - Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi

accepted.s: Who wrote the Sufi text ‘Kashf-ul-Mahjub’?
accepted.x: ‘Kashf-ul-Mahjub’ was written by Ali Hujwiri, also known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.
accepted.tq: Direct author–work recall.

accepted.s: Ali Hujwiri is particularly associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: The first prominent Sufi in India
The last great Chishti saint of Delhi
The founder of the Qadiri order in India
The compiler of the Adi Granth
accepted.x: Ali Hujwiri, or Data Ganj Bakhsh, is described as the first prominent Sufi in India.
accepted.tq: Identify the person from a distinctive title or description.

accepted.s: The principal themes of ‘Kashf-ul-Mahjub’ are which of the following?
o: Trade and taxation in the Deccan
Love and knowledge of God and fana
accepted.x: ‘Kashf-ul-Mahjub’ deals with love and knowledge of God and the concept of fana.
accepted.tq: Direct thematic recall.

accepted.s: ‘Fawaid-ul-Fuad’, a malfuzat of Nizamuddin Auliya, was recorded by whom?
accepted.x: ‘Fawaid-ul-Fuad’ was compiled by Amir Hasan Sijzi and records the conversations of Nizamuddin Auliya.
accepted.tq: Match a text with its compiler.

accepted.s: ‘Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani’ is best described as which of the following?
o: An anti-Shia tract by Abdul Haqq Dehlavi
A tazkira written by Mir Khwurd Kirmani
accepted.x: ‘Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani’ consists of the letters of Ahmad Sirhindi.
accepted.tq: Confusable text–genre discrimination.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Siyar-ul-Auliya — Mir Khwurd Kirmani
2. Akhbar-ul-Akhyar — Abdul Haqq Muhaddis Dehlavi
3. Fawaid-ul-Fuad — Ahmad Sirhindi
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: ‘Siyar-ul-Auliya’ was written by Mir Khwurd Kirmani and ‘Akhbar-ul-Akhyar’ by Abdul Haqq Muhaddis Dehlavi. ‘Fawaid-ul-Fuad’ was associated with Amir Hasan Sijzi, not Ahmad Sirhindi.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the swapped author in a statement set.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the genre ‘malfuzat’?
o: Letters written by a Sufi saint
Recorded conversations of a Sufi saint
accepted.x: Malfuzat are recorded conversations or sayings of Sufi saints.
accepted.tq: Exact-term and definition recall.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Tazkiras are biographies of saints. Anti-Shia tracts are represented by works such as ‘Radd-i-Khawafiq’.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrectly defined paired term.

accepted.s: ‘Radd-i-Khawafiq’ was authored by Ahmad Sirhindi and belongs to which category?
accepted.x: ‘Radd-i-Khawafiq’ is an anti-Shia tract associated with Ahmad Sirhindi.
accepted.tq: Direct work–type association.

accepted.s: Who is associated with the title ‘Garib Nawaz’?
accepted.x: ‘Garib Nawaz’ is the title associated with Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti.
accepted.tq: Title–saint recall.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: ‘Mahboob-i-Ilahi’ is associated with Nizamuddin Auliya. The other titles belong to Nasiruddin Mahmud, Baba Fariduddin and Ahmad Sirhindi respectively.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure title–saint pair.

accepted.s: ‘Chiragh-i-Delhi’ is associated with which Sufi saint?
accepted.x: ‘Chiragh-i-Delhi’ is associated with Nasiruddin Mahmud, the last great Chishti saint of Delhi.
accepted.tq: Direct title–person recall.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Banda Nawaz or Gesudaraz — Muhammad Hussaini Gesudaraz
accepted.x: ‘Garib Nawaz’ is associated with Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, not Nasiruddin Mahmud.
accepted.tq: Use the swapped person–title trap.

accepted.s: Who took the Chishti order to the Deccan and established its presence at Khuldabad?
accepted.x: Burhanuddin Gharib took the Chishti order to the Deccan at Khuldabad.
accepted.tq: Direct founder or transmitter recall.

accepted.s: Burhanuddin Gharib took the Chishti order to the Deccan in which century?
accepted.x: The event is dated to the 14th century, although some UPSC notes mention the 13th century.
accepted.tq: Distinguish close chronological alternatives.

accepted.s: Which of the following developments followed the movement of Chishtis towards the Deccan?
o: Abandonment of khanqahs in the Deccan
Formation of the Naqshbandi order at Delhi
Shift of the Chishti order to Ajmer alone
accepted.x: The migration of Chishtis to Gulbarga followed Burhanuddin Gharib’s transmission of the order to the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Cause-and-effect linkage.

accepted.s: The dargah of Gesudaraz, also known as Bande Nawaz, is located at which place?
accepted.x: The dargah of Gesudaraz or Bande Nawaz is at Gulbarga, where he settled under the Bahmanis.
accepted.tq: Dargah–location recall.

accepted.s: Gesudaraz settled at Gulbarga under the patronage of which ruling power?
accepted.x: Gesudaraz settled at Gulbarga under the Bahmanis.
accepted.tq: Match a saint with the relevant ruling power.

accepted.s: Which city developed into a key Chishti centre in the Deccan after Gulbarga?
accepted.x: Bijapur grew into a key Chishti centre in the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Location-based direct recall.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sufi gurus migrated to and settled in Golconda.
2. Sufism gained immense popularity in Golconda.
3. Khanqahs in Golconda served as higher-education centres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Golconda witnessed the settlement of Sufi gurus, widespread popularity of Sufism and the development of khanqahs as higher-education centres.
accepted.tq: Test a connected group of regional facts.

accepted.s: The Ameen Peer dargah, also called Asthana-e-Magdoomiya, is located at which place in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Ameen Peer dargah, or Asthana-e-Magdoomiya, is located at Kadapa.
accepted.tq: Direct shrine–place recall.

accepted.s: Which Sufi shrine is located at Penukonda in Sri Sathya Sai district?
accepted.x: The Baba Fakhruddin dargah is located at Penukonda in Sri Sathya Sai district.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related regional shrines.

accepted.s: Ameen Peer Dargah at Kadapa is associated with which saint and period?
accepted.x: The Kadapa shrine is associated with Peerullah Hussaini and dates to the 17th century.
accepted.tq: Combine person, place and period in one precise option.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is located at Penukonda, not Bijapur. Gesudaraz’s dargah is at Gulbarga.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-location trap.

accepted.s: Who among the following was the founder of the Chishti order in India according to the dargah tradition?
accepted.x: Moinuddin Chishti is identified as the founder of the Chishti order in India.
accepted.tq: Direct founder identification.

accepted.s: The dargah of Moinuddin Chishti is situated at which place?
accepted.x: Moinuddin Chishti’s dargah is at Ajmer.
accepted.tq: Saint–dargah location recall.

accepted.s: Who among the following was born in 1173 and died in 1235, with his dargah at Delhi?
accepted.x: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki lived from 1173 to 1235 and his dargah is at Delhi, specifically Mehrauli.
accepted.tq: Use dates to distinguish closely associated saints.

accepted.s: Baba Farid’s dargah is located at Ajodhan, which is also known as:
accepted.x: Ajodhan, the location of Baba Farid’s dargah, is also known as Pakpattan.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between alternative names of a place.

accepted.s: Which Chishti saint’s verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib or Adi Granth?
accepted.x: Verses of Baba Farid are included in the Guru Granth Sahib, also called the Adi Granth.
accepted.tq: Associate a literary contribution with its author.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Nizamuddin Auliya:
1. His dargah is located in Delhi.
2. He was born at Badaun.
3. He was a disciple of Baba Farid.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Nizamuddin Auliya’s dargah is in Delhi; he was born at Badaun and was a disciple of Baba Farid.
accepted.tq: Combine place, lineage and shrine facts.

accepted.s: Who was the last great Chishti saint of Delhi?
accepted.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud, known as Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, was the last great Chishti saint of Delhi.
accepted.tq: Test a first/last distinction.

accepted.s: The dargah of Salim Chishti is located at:
accepted.x: Salim Chishti’s dargah is at Fatehpur Sikri, and he is associated with Akbar.
accepted.tq: Dargah–location recall.

accepted.s: Which Chishti saint is associated with Akbar?
accepted.x: Salim Chishti is identified as Akbar’s saint and is associated with Fatehpur Sikri.
accepted.tq: Ruler–saint association.

accepted.s: Amir Khusrau, the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, introduced which element of Qawwali?
o: Fana, the final stage of spiritual union
accepted.x: Amir Khusrau introduced Qaul, the opening hymn of Qawwali.
accepted.tq: Associate a cultural contribution with its contributor.

accepted.s: What is the principal distinction between Ba-shara and Be-shara Sufi orders?
o: Ba-shara orders rejected Islamic law, whereas Be-shara orders followed it strictly.
Ba-shara orders followed Islamic law, whereas Be-shara orders were not bound by it.
Ba-shara orders were confined to the Deccan, whereas Be-shara orders were confined to Delhi.
Ba-shara orders were literary groups, whereas Be-shara orders were military groups.
accepted.x: Ba-shara orders followed Sharia, while Be-shara orders were not bound by Islamic law. Both types coexisted in India.
accepted.tq: Test the exact contrast between paired categories.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a Ba-shara Sufi order?
accepted.x: The Qalandars were wandering Be-shara groups. Chishti, Suhrawardi and Qadiri were Ba-shara orders.
accepted.tq: Find the odd category in a listed group.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Naqshbandi — Ba-shara
2. Firdausi — Ba-shara
3. Madaris — Be-shara
4. Qalandars — Be-shara
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Naqshbandi and Firdausi are Ba-shara orders, while Madaris and wandering Qalandars are Be-shara groups. Hence all four pairs are correct.
accepted.tq: Classify every item before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Which comparison between the Chishti and Suhrawardi orders is correct?
o: Chishtis were close to the court, whereas Suhrawardis rejected sama entirely.
Chishtis were the orthodox pole, whereas Suhrawardis were wandering Qalandars.
Chishtis were generally aloof and associated with sama, whereas Suhrawardis maintained closeness to the court.
Both orders were Be-shara and rejected Islamic law.
accepted.x: The Chishtis are contrasted with the Suhrawardis as relatively aloof and associated with sama, while the Suhrawardis were closer to the court.
accepted.tq: Use the central contrast rather than a shared feature.

accepted.s: Which Sufi order is regarded as the orthodox pole in the comparative understanding of Indian Sufism?
accepted.x: The Naqshbandi order is identified as the orthodox pole in the comparison of Indian Sufi traditions.
accepted.tq: Direct identification of the contrasting category.

accepted.s: Which of the following best expresses the social and cultural significance of Sufism in India?
o: It restricted religious interaction to Persian-speaking court elites.
It eliminated the use of local languages and music in religious life.
It functioned exclusively as a military organisation.
It gave Islam a tolerant, vernacular face and made khanqahs welfare centres.
accepted.x: Sufism gave Islam in India a tolerant and vernacular character, while khanqahs served as welfare centres.
accepted.tq: Apply the broader social significance to a description.

accepted.s: Why is Chishti adaptation to local language and music considered important?
o: It separated Sufism from Indian society.
It converted all khanqahs into military cantonments.
It helped Sufism become a bridge for Indo-Islamic composite culture.
It made the Chishti order exclusively court-centred.
accepted.x: The adaptation of Chishtis to local language and music helped Sufism serve as a bridge for Indo-Islamic composite culture.
accepted.tq: Identify the cultural consequence of a stated practice.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly reflects the religious character of the dargahs at Kadapa and Penukonda?
o: They admit only members of Ba-shara orders.
They function only as higher-education centres.
They draw devotees from every community.
They are exclusively associated with the Bahmani court.
accepted.x: The dargahs at Kadapa and Penukonda draw devotees belonging to every community.
accepted.tq: Apply a general social principle to the Andhra examples.

accepted.s: Which of the following regional associations is correctly matched?
o: Golconda — Sufi patronage and the Tana Shah–Shah Raju link
accepted.x: Golconda is associated with Sufi patronage and the Tana Shah–Shah Raju link. The other shrine-location pairs are incorrect.
accepted.tq: Match the regional centre with its distinctive association.

accepted.s: Which pair represents the correct first-and-last sequence in the specified Sufi context?
o: Ali Hujwiri — first prominent Sufi in India; Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi — last great Chishti of Delhi
Moinuddin Chishti — first prominent Sufi in India; Salim Chishti — last great Chishti of Delhi
Ahmad Sirhindi — first prominent Sufi in India; Baba Farid — last great Chishti of Delhi
Burhanuddin Gharib — first prominent Sufi in India; Gesudaraz — last great Chishti of Delhi
accepted.x: Ali Hujwiri is identified as the first prominent Sufi in India, while Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi is the last great Chishti saint of Delhi.
accepted.tq: Use the first/last clues to split the options.
